The way a user asks a Nostr relay for an invite code was deleted from the spec this week, and the replacement is an endpoint only the relay operator can call.

Three pull requests merged into nostr-protocol/nips between 17:16 UTC on 23 September 2026 and 01:14 UTC on 24 September. NIP-86, the relay management API, went from 25 methods to 32. PR #2477 added unallowevent, unbanevent, listallowedevents and listdisallowedkinds. PR #2481 rewrote the file, 202 additions and 87 deletions. PR #2408 added listclaims, createclaim and deleteclaim, and removed seventeen lines from NIP-43: the entire Invite Request section, which defined a kind 28935 event the relay signed with the pubkey in its NIP-11 self field.

NIP-86 runs over HTTP and returns 401 without a valid NIP-98 event in the Authorization header. So the sentence that replaced those seventeen lines, telling users to request a claim via createclaim, points at a door users cannot open.

The rewrite also wrote down something the document never stated: banning a pubkey should remove it from the allow list, but unbanning should not add it back. Allow and ban are not two positions of one switch. An entry can sit on neither.

We read every pull request merged into the NIPs repository by merge date rather than creation date, which is the only reason a pull request opened in July and merged at 01:14 this morning appears here at all. When your relay bans a pubkey, do you know which list it lands on?

The honest limit: NIP-86 contains no uppercase RFC 2119 keywords at all, so every one of these is a lowercase should. And NIP-43 still tells clients they MUST only request kind 28935 events from relays advertising the NIP, an event no longer defined anywhere in the file.

nostr:
NIP-86 went from 25 methods to 32 in eight hours on 23 and 24 September 2026.

PR #2477 added unallowevent, unbanevent, listallowedevents, listdisallowedkinds. PR #2481 rewrote the file with a description per method, 202 additions and 87 deletions. PR #2408 added listclaims, createclaim, deleteclaim and deleted NIP-43's Invite Request section, the kind 28935 event a user requested from the relay.

The replacement sentence tells users to call createclaim. That method sits behind NIP-86's NIP-98 Authorization header, which returns 401 to anyone who is not the operator.

NIP-43 still says clients MUST only request kind 28935 events from relays advertising the NIP. That event is no longer defined in the file.
